video_description:
Going back from HyperOS 3 to HyperOS 2 on a Xiaomi or POCO phone - the official fastboot ROM route, step by step, and the one flash option you must never touch.

Let's be blunt, HyperOS 3 isn't for everyone. If battery drain, heating or a stubborn bug has you missing HyperOS 2, you can go back, and you don't need a custom ROM to do it. You need an unlocked bootloader, a full backup, and about twenty minutes. This is a fastboot ROM flash through Mi Flash Tool, which means a clean slate - your internal storage is gone. The single most important thing in the whole process is the option at the bottom of the tool. Pick Clean all. Never pick Clean all and lock. That setting relocks the bootloader mid-flash, and that's how phones end up dead on the desk.

📱 Device  : Xiaomi and POCO phones on HyperOS
🧩 ROM     : Official HyperOS 2 fastboot ROM (your exact model)
🛠️ Tools   : Mi Flash Tool, ADB and fastboot driver
🧨 Risk    : Full data wipe · unlocked bootloader required

🛠️ What You Need
• The HyperOS 2 fastboot ROM for your exact model and region, not another phone's file
• Mi Flash Tool installed on a Windows PC
• ADB and fastboot driver and a cable that isn't falling apart
• Your bootloader unlocked
• A full backup taken off the phone
• Enough charge to get through the flash

📝 Steps
1. Download the correct HyperOS 2 fastboot ROM and extract it.
2. Power the phone off, then hold Volume Down and Power for fastboot.
3. Connect it to the PC and check it's detected.
4. Open Mi Flash Tool and select the extracted ROM folder.
5. At the bottom, choose Clean all. Not Clean all and lock.
6. Hit refresh so the tool sees your device.
7. Hit flash and leave the cable alone.
8. When it finishes, the phone boots straight into HyperOS 2.

⚠️ Where People Get Stuck
• Picking Clean all and lock. That relocks the bootloader mid-flash and can leave you with a phone you can't recover easily.
• Using a ROM for the wrong model or region. It stalls halfway, or worse.
• Skipping the backup because it's "only a rollback". It erases internal storage.

❓ Common Questions
• Will I lose my data? Yes, everything.
